messages:
maya: Hey support — customer `acme-marketing` reports their embeddings job started failing this morning. Getting a dimension_mismatch error and huge tail latency. Posting logs + repro below. Anyone seen this pattern?

eli: Ping @oncall. Can you take a look? They say it worked yesterday.

oncall: On it. Can you paste an example request and the exact error?

maya: Sure. Repro curl we ran against the embeddings endpoint in us-east-1: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-1536","input":["a short sentence"],"batch_size":1}'
```
Response: `{"error":"dimension_mismatch","expected":1536,"got":768}`

sam: That error usually means the client is hitting a model variant with different vector size — either wrong model id or routing sent it to a smaller model. Could be quantized embed-768 behind the scenes.

eli: Do we have routing logs for that request? @infra-bot any traces?

infra-bot: Trace ID f2a9c1. Request routed to host embed-proxy-07 in eu-west-1 because us-east pool was cold and spillover policy kicked in.

maya: Wait — the curl had X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1. Why did it go to eu-west-1?

infra-bot: Routing policy: region_fallback=auto, prefer_region=true, max_pending=200. At 06:12:14 UTC the us-east warm pool had 0 ready replicas -> autoscaler requested startup; routing allowed spillover to nearest region defined in topology: eu-west-1. Embed model versions differ between regions (1536 vs 768).

oncall: That explains dimension mismatch. Latency spike because cross-region and cold starts. Did customer see many retries?

maya: Yes, they retried with exponential backoff; billing shows a bump in token billing and embedding units. @billing-bot can you confirm if retries got charged twice?

billing-bot: Looks like 18 duplicate requests billed between 06:12–06:18 UTC for acme-marketing; chargeback recommended if we waive.

sam: Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Pin region in request via X-Redwood-Region and also set a hard_route flag to disable spillover for this customer.
- If pinning isn't possible client-side, apply customer-specific routing rule to prefer us-east-only for acme-marketing.
- Warm pools: increase min_ready for embed-1536 in us-east to avoid cold starts.

eli: Repro steps for engineering to replicate locally:
1) Set routing to allow_spillover=true and reduce us-east warm pool to 0.
2) Send embed-1536 request with region header us-east and observe trace.
3) Confirm response from eu-west shows model id embed-768.

maya: Attaching server log excerpt (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-12T06:12:13Z] TRACE f2a9c1 ingress: recv req customer=acme-marketing region=us-east-1
[2026-03-12T06:12:13Z] INFO routing: us-east pool_ready=0 spillover=eu-west-1
[2026-03-12T06:12:13Z] INFO proxy: forwarded to eu-west-1/embed-node-14 model=embed-768
[2026-03-12T06:12:14Z] ERROR model: dimension_mismatch expected=1536 got=768
[2026-03-12T06:12:14Z] WARN ingest: retry from client backoff=500ms
```

oncall: Can we confirm why eu-west had embed-768 while us-east has embed-1536? Shouldn't model catalog be consistent?

infra-bot: Catalog drift detected for model `embed-1536` between regions. eu-west catalog marks alias embed-1536 -> embed-quant-768 (compat override). A deployment job rolled a quantized build in eu-west last night.

sam: Root cause: catalog drift + permissive spillover routing + low warm pool in us-east.

eli: Next steps I propose:
- Short term (minutes): Pin routing for acme-marketing to us-east-only; waive duplicate charges and notify customer.
- Short term (hours): Roll back quant-768 alias in eu-west or ensure alias resolves to 1536-shape variant.
- Medium term: Add validation in routing layer to check vector shape compatibility before forwarding; fail fast with 409 and clear error instead of sending to incompatible model.
- Medium term: Add audit alert when catalog alias resolution differs across regions.

maya: Can infra do the pinning now?

infra-bot: I applied temporary route override: customer=acme-marketing -> region=us-east-1 hard=true at 2026-03-12T06:34:21Z. Warm pool scale request submitted to autoscaler for embed-1536 us-east min_ready=2.

maya: Thx. I'll notify the customer and offer a billing credit.

billing-bot: Billing hold placed pending manual review; suggested credit $45 for duplicate requests.

sam: For the follow-up ticket to eng-runtime: include the log excerpt, trace id f2a9c1, and a repro toggle to simulate catalog drift so QA can verify the fail-fast behavior.

eli: I'll open the runtime ticket and assign to @sam and @maya for triage.

maya: Customer updated: they confirmed error stopped after we pinned region. They're okay with credit and a post-mortem. I'll collect timestamps and user request ids.

oncall: Excellent. Closing loop: add test in e2e to ensure emb shapes are consistent or routing rejects on mismatch. :white_check_mark:

sam: Also consider a metric for "routing_shape_mismatch" to alert before it affects many customers.

maya: Thanks all. I'll put the postmortem draft in #postmortems once we have the timeline.

infra-bot: Autoscaler status: scale up in progress -> 2 replicas ready expected within 90s.

eli: If anything else pops up tag @oncall immediately.

oncall: Thanks team.
